newsitem.title: UK: Stocks fall in London, Tokyo.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall in London, Tokyo.

text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - The benchmark FTSE 100 share index registered its biggest one-day drop in 2-1/2 months as worries about the contents of the British budget preoccupied investors. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,682.2, down 62.9 points, or 1.33 percent.

FRANKFURT - Stocks ended bourse trade sharply lower amid nervous market sentiment with no new data around to help lift spirits on the floor of the Frankfurt bourse. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,741.48, down 23.63 points, or 0.63 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,721.18, down 28.84 points, or 0.77 percent.

PARIS - Stocks fell sharply on profit-taking fuelled by Wall Street's drop and caution ahead of the new Socialist-led government's keynote policy speech on Thursday. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,762.60, down 33.27 points, or 1.19 percent.

ZURICH - Shares closed lower after strong U.S. May industrial production data led to a fall on Wall Street, dragging most European bourses down with it, dealers said. The Swiss market index closed at 5,345.9, down 16.1 points, or 0.30 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks ended with losses, slipping on the strengthening yen against the dollar, brokers said. They said investors were sidelined ahead of Japan's May customs-cleared trade data due Wednesday and the G7 summit later this week. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,593.66, down 87.41 points, or 0.42 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed lower in cautious trading with investors concerned about possible curbs on local property prices. The Hang Seng index closed at 14,307.15, down 87.45 points, or 0.61 percent.

SYDNEY - Stocks ended at a record closing high after speculation over a South African takeover of Australia's second largest nickel producer prompted heavy trading in the resources sector. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,681.7, up 12.4 points, or 0.46 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares ended down as futures traders, mindful of the Friday close-out date on near-dated June contracts, pushed the market into negative territory. The All-share index closed at 7,192.1, down 79.4 points, or 1.09 percent. The All Gold index closed at 1,100.5, down 28.4 points, or 0.59 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,432.7, down 49.7 points, or 2.52 percent.
